    cs-host|contains: '39.107.60.51'
    cs-uri-stem|contains: '/api/software/'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationIp:39.107.60.51 @DestinationPort:80
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4=39.107.60.51 RemotePort=80
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.dest="39.107.60.51" OR Web.url="*/api/software/*") Web.http_method="POST" by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.http_method, Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.dest="39.107.60.51" OR Web.url="*/api/software/*") Web.http_method="POST" by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.http_method, Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Malicious JetBrains Marketplace plugin ID present in IDE plugins folder AIInstallation High
All 15 IoC plugin XML ids (org.sm.yms.toolkit, com.json.simple.kit, com.my.code.tools, ord.cp.code.ai.kit, etc.) are distinctive enough that any file write under %APPDATA%\JetBrains\<IDE>\plugins or ~/.config/JetBrains/<IDE>/plugins that contains one of these identifiers is conclusive evidence the host installed a backdoored plugin from the campaign. This catches the install moment regardless of whether the user has yet pasted an AI API key. Rationale: Plugin XML ids are the canonical, unique identifier JetBrains uses to dedupe Marketplace entries; the 15 ids in the article's IoC table are the verbatim package identifiers and will be present on disk in any installed copy (Marketplace install writes them into the plugin's META-INF). High-fidelity with effectively zero collision risk.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1505.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Endpoint forensics tool re-reading a quarantined plugin artifact
  • Backup software touching the JetBrains plugins directory and re-emitting filenames
  • Developer manually examining a benign plugin coincidentally named identically (improbable — these ids are squatted attacker-chosen strings)
  • Security inventory scanner enumerating installed plugin metadata
Response runbook
1) Triage: enumerate every plugin under %APPDATA%\JetBrains (Win) or ~/Library/Application Support/JetBrains (mac) or ~/.config/JetBrains (Linux) on the host; cross-reference plugin.xml id against the 15 IoCs; pull DeviceNetworkEvents for that host to confirm whether 39.107.60.51 was already contacted (key already exfil'd). 2) Contain: uninstall the plugin via JetBrains Plugins UI (Disable → Restart → Remove), then delete the residual directory; rotate any AI provider API keys that user has used in the IDE in the last 90 days; push EDR-level block for the plugin id strings. 3) Hunt: sweep the entire developer fleet with the same query over 60d to find every infected host; cross-reference vendor accounts (CodePilot/mycode, StackSmith/misshewei, CodeCrafter/keteme, CodeWeaver/simpledev, JetCode/skyblue, DailyCode/dialycode, ZenCoder/947cb4c8-5db1-4cf0-8182-0aae7c433bb3) for any future plugin uploads.
let MaliciousPluginIds = dynamic(["org.sm.yms.toolkit","com.json.simple.kit","org.bug.find.tools","org.translate.ai.simple","com.yy.test.ai.simple","com.dev.ai.toolkit","com.json.view.simple","com.my.git.ai.kit","org.check.ai.ds","com.review.tool.code","org.code.assist.dev.tool","com.coder.ai.dpt","com.my.code.tools","ord.cp.code.ai.kit","com.dp.git.ai.tool"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where FolderPath has "JetBrains" and FolderPath has "plugins"
| where FileName has_any (MaliciousPluginIds) or FolderPath has_any (MaliciousPluginIds)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'

falsepositives:

level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user

Critical

Google Vertex AI SDK Flaw Let Attackers Hijack Model Uploads via Bucket Squatting

The Hacker News
2026-06-16 9 use cases 4 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

A flaw in the Google Cloud Vertex AI SDK for Python let an attacker with no access to a victim's project hijack the victim's machine learning model upload and run code inside Google's serving infrastructure. Palo Alto Networks Unit 42, which found and reported the bug through Google's bug bounty program, calls the technique "Pickle in the Middle" and said it saw no exploitation in the wild.

CVEsCVE-2026-2473
ATT&CKT1190 T1528 T1555.003 T1566

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Vulnerable google-cloud-aiplatform SDK (<1.148.0) on managed endpoints · [LLM] Pip/uv/poetry installing vulnerable google-cloud-aiplatform (<1.148.0)
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Vertex AI predictable staging-bucket pattern created in GCP (default-path use) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Vulnerable google-cloud-aiplatform SDK (<1.148.0) on managed endpoints AIWeaponization High
Hunts hosts (workstations, CI runners, Vertex AI Workbench / notebook VMs reporting into Defender) carrying google-cloud-aiplatform older than 1.148.0 — the version that adds bucket-ownership verification against the 'Pickle in the Middle' bucket-squatting flaw. Pure asset-hygiene hunt; finds the systems that need patching before adversaries weaponise the predictable staging-bucket naming. Rationale: Article names the exact patched version (1.148.0 on April 15 2026, partial fix 1.144.0 on March 31) and stresses checking google-cloud-aiplatform wherever it runs — workstations, notebooks, CI, training pipelines. Defender's DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory is the cleanest single-shot pivot. Sentinel/Datadog/Falcon/CloudWatch left empty: there is no equivalent first-class Python-package inventory column in those schemas (Sentinel's DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities depends on a CveId which the article notes is not assigned).
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Engineering workstations intentionally pinned to an older SDK for reproducibility of a model that was trained against that release
  • Vertex AI Workbench notebook images shipped by Google that haven't been refreshed since the user provisioned them
  • CI runner base images baked weeks/months ago and not yet rebuilt against the latest pin
  • Air-gapped or offline dev VMs that can't reach PyPI to upgrade
  • Vendor-managed ML platforms (Kubeflow / Vertex Pipelines containers) that bundle their own SDK version
Suppression filter
| where SoftwareVersion !startswith "1.148" and SoftwareVersion !startswith "1.149" and not (SoftwareVersion matches regex @"^1\.(1[5-9][0-9]|[2-9][0-9]{2})\.")
Response runbook
Triage: pull the device's full Python environment inventory and confirm google-cloud-aiplatform version + which user/project_id it's authenticated against; check whether staging_bucket is set explicitly in the codebase (grep for `aiplatform.init`, `Model.upload`, `staging_bucket=`). Contain: pin the requirements file to >=1.148.0 and force `pip install --upgrade google-cloud-aiplatform`; if the host has uploaded models via Model.upload in the last 30 days, rotate any GCP service-account credentials it used. Hunt: enumerate all GCP project IDs the host has touched and audit each project for buckets matching `<project>-vertex-staging-<region>` ownership.
DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
| where SoftwareName =~ "google-cloud-aiplatform"
| extend Parts = split(SoftwareVersion, ".")
| extend Major = toint(tostring(Parts[0])), Minor = toint(tostring(Parts[1])), Patch = toint(tostring(Parts[2]))
| where (Major < 1) or (Major == 1 and Minor < 148)
| project DeviceName, DeviceId, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, OSPlatform, Major, Minor, Patch
| order by DeviceName asc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(Endpoint.Processes.process) as cmdlines, max(_time) as lastSeen from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Endpoint.Processes.process_name IN ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","pip","pip3","pip3.10","pip3.11","pip3.12","uv.exe","uv","poetry.exe","conda.exe") AND Endpoint.Processes.process="*google-cloud-aiplatform*" by host, user | `drop_dm_object_name(Endpoint.Processes)` | rex field=cmdlines "google-cloud-aiplatform[=<\s]*(?<version>\d+\.\d+\.\d+)" | rex field=version "(?<major>\d+)\.(?<minor>\d+)\.(?<patch>\d+)" | where major<1 OR (major=1 AND minor<148) | table host, user, version, lastSeen, cmdlines
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Endpoint.Processes.process) as cmdlines, max(_time) as lastSeen from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Endpoint.Processes.process_name IN ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","pip","pip3","pip3.10","pip3.11","pip3.12","uv.exe","uv","poetry.exe","conda.exe") AND Endpoint.Processes.process="*google-cloud-aiplatform*" by host, user | `drop_dm_object_name(Endpoint.Processes)` | rex field=cmdlines "google-cloud-aiplatform[=<\s]*(?<version>\d+\.\d+\.\d+)" | rex field=version "(?<major>\d+)\.(?<minor>\d+)\.(?<patch>\d+)" | where major<1 OR (major=1 AND minor<148) | table host, user, version, lastSeen, cmdlines
Pip/uv/poetry installing vulnerable google-cloud-aiplatform (<1.148.0) AIWeaponization High
Hunts process executions where pip / uv / poetry / conda install or upgrade google-cloud-aiplatform to a vulnerable version (anything below 1.148.0, which added bucket-ownership verification for Model.upload). Catches CI jobs, notebook %pip cells, and dev workstations actively pulling the unpatched SDK so the SOC can flag the owning team before they trigger the bucket-squat scenario. Rationale: Article gives precise patched-version cutoffs (1.144.0 partial, 1.148.0 full) and explicitly tells defenders to check the SDK 'wherever it runs, including notebooks, CI jobs, and training pipelines.' Pip/uv/poetry install command lines are the highest-fidelity active-install signal across endpoint EDRs. Regex tolerates unpinned installs (latest at time of run could still be vulnerable) by allowing empty PinnedVersion through.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • CI/CD reproducibility pins to a specific old release for a model that was trained on that version
  • Notebook %pip cells copied from old tutorials still hard-coding 1.139.0 / 1.140.0
  • Migration playbooks that install old then upgrade in a second step
  • Vendor templates (Kubeflow, training-image base layers) bundling an older google-cloud-aiplatform pin
  • `pip install -r requirements.txt` where the file pins old versions — the install fires our detection on every CI run until the lockfile is updated
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains "\\GitHub Actions\\" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("runner.exe","Runner.Worker.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: pull the parent process + working directory; identify whether this was a one-off dev install vs a recurring CI build vs a notebook execution. Pull the requirements file or pipeline definition to see if the pin is deliberate. Contain: open a ticket against the owning team to upgrade the pin to >=1.148.0; if the run produced a successful Model.upload(), inventory the GCP project_id + region used and verify the staging bucket is owned by the expected project. Hunt: pivot to all hosts that ran the same vulnerable version in the last 30 days, and to any Cloud Build / GitHub Actions runners executing similar pipelines.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","pip","pip3","pip3.10","pip3.11","pip3.12","uv.exe","uv","poetry.exe","conda.exe")
   or (FileName in~ ("python.exe","python3","python") and ProcessCommandLine has "-m pip")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "install" and ProcessCommandLine has "google-cloud-aiplatform"
| extend PinnedVersion = extract(@"google-cloud-aiplatform[=<~\s]*(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| extend Major = toint(extract(@"^(\d+)\.", 1, PinnedVersion)),
         Minor = toint(extract(@"^\d+\.(\d+)\.", 1, PinnedVersion))
| where isempty(PinnedVersion) or (Major < 1) or (Major == 1 and Minor < 148)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountUpn, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, PinnedVersion, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\pip.exe","\\pip3.exe","\\uv.exe","\\poetry.exe","\\conda.exe") 
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\\python.exe" and CommandLine has "-m pip")
| where CommandLine has "install" and CommandLine has "google-cloud-aiplatform"
| extend PinnedVersion = extract(@"google-cloud-aiplatform[=<~\s]*(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, CommandLine)
| extend Major = toint(extract(@"^(\d+)\.", 1, PinnedVersion)),
         Minor = toint(extract(@"^\d+\.(\d+)\.", 1, PinnedVersion))
| where isempty(PinnedVersion) or (Major < 1) or (Major == 1 and Minor < 148)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, PinnedVersion, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Pip Install of Vulnerable google-cloud-aiplatform SDK (Pickle in the Middle)
id: 9b6d7a2c-3f4e-4d2b-b8e1-6a5c1f3d9e22
status: experimental
description: Detects pip / uv / poetry / conda installing the Vertex AI SDK at a version below 1.148.0 — the fix for the bucket-squatting Pickle-in-the-Middle flaw (Palo Alto Unit 42, Jun 2026).
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/google-vertex-ai-sdk-flaw-let-attackers.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1059.006
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_installer:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\pip.exe'
      - '\pip3.exe'
      - '\uv.exe'
      - '\poetry.exe'
      - '\conda.exe'
  selection_pymod:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\python3.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '-m pip'
  selection_target:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'install'
      - 'google-cloud-aiplatform'
  condition: (selection_installer or selection_pymod) and selection_target
falsepositives:
  - Reproducibility pins in long-lived CI pipelines
  - Notebook templates still referencing pre-1.148.0
level: medium

(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) (@Image:(*\pip.exe OR *\pip3.exe OR *\uv.exe OR *\poetry.exe OR *\conda.exe) OR @process.executable.path:(*/pip OR */pip3 OR */uv OR */poetry OR */conda)) (@CommandLine:(*install*google-cloud-aiplatform* OR *google-cloud-aiplatform*install*) OR @process.command_line:(*install*google-cloud-aiplatform* OR *google-cloud-aiplatform*install*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(pip3?|uv|poetry|conda)\.exe$/i OR ImageFileName=/\/(pip3?|uv|poetry|conda)$/i
| CommandLine=/install/i
| CommandLine=/google-cloud-aiplatform/i
| regex("google-cloud-aiplatform[=<~\\s]*(?<pinned>\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+)", field=CommandLine, strict=false)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, pinned], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, values(Endpoint.Processes.process) as cmdlines from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Endpoint.Processes.process_name IN ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","pip","pip3","pip3.10","pip3.11","pip3.12","uv.exe","uv","poetry.exe","conda.exe","python.exe","python3") AND Endpoint.Processes.process="*google-cloud-aiplatform*" AND Endpoint.Processes.process="*install*" by host, user, Endpoint.Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Endpoint.Processes)` | rex field=cmdlines "google-cloud-aiplatform[=<~\s]*(?<pinned>\d+\.\d+\.\d+)" | rex field=pinned "(?<major>\d+)\.(?<minor>\d+)\.(?<patch>\d+)" | where major<1 OR (major=1 AND minor<148) | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, values(Endpoint.Processes.process) as cmdlines from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Endpoint.Processes.process_name IN ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","pip","pip3","pip3.10","pip3.11","pip3.12","uv.exe","uv","poetry.exe","conda.exe","python.exe","python3") AND Endpoint.Processes.process="*google-cloud-aiplatform*" AND Endpoint.Processes.process="*install*" by host, user, Endpoint.Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Endpoint.Processes)` | rex field=cmdlines "google-cloud-aiplatform[=<~\s]*(?<pinned>\d+\.\d+\.\d+)" | rex field=pinned "(?<major>\d+)\.(?<minor>\d+)\.(?<patch>\d+)" | where major<1 OR (major=1 AND minor<148) | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Vertex AI predictable staging-bucket pattern created in GCP (default-path use) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts Cloud Storage bucket-create events in monitored GCP projects where the bucket name matches the Vertex AI SDK's predictable default pattern `<project>-vertex-staging-<region>`. Every hit is a Vertex AI workflow relying on the unsafe default — exactly the precondition the bucket-squat attack needs. Lets the SOC find owning teams and push them onto an explicit staging_bucket they control. Rationale: Article specifies the exact predictable name shape `project-vertex-staging-region` and identifies 'staging_bucket parameter unset' as one of two preconditions for the attack. The bucket-name regex `-vertex-staging-<region>` is a direct read of that article-specific string. CloudWatch left empty (GCP, not AWS). Falcon LogScale left empty: GCP audit logs don't naturally flow into FDR. Defender CloudAppEvents only fires if Defender for Cloud Apps is connected to GCP — included as best-effort.
ATT&CKT1583.006 T1648
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Brand-new Vertex AI Workbench notebook in a brand-new project (legitimate first-time SDK use)
  • ML platform teams provisioning the bucket explicitly via Terraform/Pulumi to pre-claim the name (a deliberate countermeasure)
  • Reused training pipelines that have always relied on the SDK default and pre-date the patch advisory
  • Cross-region expansion: same team adding a new region and the SDK creates `<existing-project>-vertex-staging-<new-region>`
  • Vertex Pipelines / Kubeflow components creating staging buckets on behalf of users via the default path
Suppression filter
| where not (ProjectPrefix == ProjectId)
Response runbook
Triage: pull the principal email + caller IP from the audit event; confirm the bucket lives in the same project_id its prefix names (this is the squat-detection check — `project_prefix == project_id`). If yes, fine but vulnerable; if no, it's an active squat. Contain: if same-project, message the owning team to set an explicit `staging_bucket=` they control and upgrade google-cloud-aiplatform to >=1.148.0; if cross-project, the bucket is hostile — block the SDK runtime's egress and rotate any uploaded model artifacts. Hunt: enumerate all Model.upload() runs in the affected project for the last 30 days; pull each uploaded model artifact's SHA256 and verify against the expected training output.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application has "Google" and ActionType in~ ("storage.buckets.create","CreateBucket","google.storage.v1.Storage.CreateBucket")
| extend BucketName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).resourceName)
| extend BucketName = iff(isempty(BucketName), tostring(ObjectName), BucketName)
| where BucketName matches regex @"-vertex-staging-[a-z0-9-]+$"
| project Timestamp, Application, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, CountryCode, ActionType, BucketName, ObjectId, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
GCPAuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where MethodName in ("storage.buckets.create","google.storage.v1.Storage.CreateBucket")
| extend BucketName = tostring(parse_json(ResourceName).resourceName)
| extend BucketName = iff(isempty(BucketName), extract(@"buckets/([^/]+)", 1, tostring(ResourceName)), BucketName)
| where BucketName matches regex @"-vertex-staging-[a-z0-9-]+$"
| extend ProjectPrefix = extract(@"^(.+)-vertex-staging-", 1, BucketName),
         Region = extract(@"-vertex-staging-([a-z0-9-]+)$", 1, BucketName)
| project TimeGenerated, PrincipalEmail, CallerIp, ProjectId, BucketName, ProjectPrefix, Region, MethodName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental

Hitting this default means the workflow did not set an explicit staging_bucket — the precondition for the Unit 42 'Pickle in the Middle' bucket-squat attack.

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"

BleepingComputer

Threat actors are abusing Steam Workshop, Valve's community hub for downloading game-related content, to push various malware hidden in wallpaper packages. [...]

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Article-specific behavioural hunt — Steam Workshop abused to spread malware via Wallpaper Engine app
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Wallpaper Engine spawning unexpected child process from Steam Workshop content directory · [LLM] AggregatorHost.dll loaded from non-System32 path (Steam credential stealer sideload) · [LLM] Known DarkKomet / Wallpaper-Engine campaign payload hash execution or write · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound connection to Steam Workshop wallpaper campaign C2 (202.144.192.29 / 120.48.156.17 / brightly.to) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Non-Steam process reading Steam sentry / loginusers credential files · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Wallpaper Engine spawning unexpected child process from Steam Workshop content directory AIInstallation High
Detects Wallpaper Engine (wallpaper32.exe / wallpaper64.exe) spawning a child process whose image resides under the Steam Workshop content directory for Wallpaper Engine (app id 431960). Per Kaspersky, malicious 'application'-type wallpapers auto-execute bundled payloads at install — this is the core execution telemetry shape. Rationale: Pulls the article's specific parent binaries (Wallpaper Engine's wallpaper32.exe/wallpaper64.exe) and the Wallpaper Engine Steam Workshop app id 431960 path. Cross-checked Steam app id from public Steam Wallpaper Engine page and SteamDB. Cross-checked against: • https://store.steampowered.com/app/431960/Wallpaper_Engine/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate 'application' wallpapers (system monitors, widget apps) installed by power users that the security team has not vetted
  • Wallpaper Engine self-update spawning its own installer from the Steam apps directory (parent path mismatch but similar shape)
  • Crash reporting via WerFault.exe being launched from the Workshop content folder
  • Developers testing their own Workshop submissions on dev workstations
Suppression filter
| where not (FileName in~ ("WerFault.exe","WerFaultSecure.exe","dllhost.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "services.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the ChildImage SHA256/MD5 and cross-reference against the article's MD5 list and threat-intel; pull the Workshop content sub-folder (the numeric id after 431960 is the Workshop item id — look it up on steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=<id> to see the wallpaper name/author). 2) Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response or EDR network containment, kill the child process tree, remove the Workshop subscription via steam://url/CommunityFilePage/<id> when ready. 3) Hunt: pivot on the SHA256/MD5 across the fleet for other hosts with the same wallpaper, then run UC2/UC3/UC4 (AggregatorHost.dll sideload, Steam credential file access, C2 IPs) against the same DeviceId for the next 24h to surface follow-on stages.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wallpaper32.exe","wallpaper64.exe")
| where FolderPath has @"\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has @"\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\"
| where FileName !in~ ("wallpaper32.exe","wallpaper64.exe","webwallpaper32.exe","webwallpaper64.exe","conhost.exe","WerFault.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildImage=FolderPath, ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, MD5
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\wallpaper32.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\wallpaper64.exe"
| where NewProcessName has @"\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\" or CommandLine has @"\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\"
| where NewProcessName !endswith "\\wallpaper32.exe" and NewProcessName !endswith "\\wallpaper64.exe" and NewProcessName !endswith "\\conhost.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Wallpaper Engine Spawning Child From Steam Workshop Content Directory
id: 5d7b5e4a-8a13-4d57-9e2c-31b8f1c4b2d4
description: Detects Wallpaper Engine spawning a child process whose image lives under the Wallpaper Engine Steam Workshop content folder (app id 431960).
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/steam-workshop-abused-to-spread-malware-via-wallpaper-engine-app/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\wallpaper32.exe'
      - '\wallpaper64.exe'
  selection_path:
    Image|contains: '\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\wallpaper32.exe'
      - '\wallpaper64.exe'
      - '\conhost.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_path and not filter_legit
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\wallpaper32.exe OR *\wallpaper64.exe OR *\Wallpaper32.exe OR *\Wallpaper64.exe) (@Image:*\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\* OR @CommandLine:*\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\*) -@Image:(*\wallpaper32.exe OR *\wallpaper64.exe OR *\conhost.exe OR *\WerFault.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/wallpaper(32|64)\.exe$/i
| regex("\\\\steamapps\\\\workshop\\\\content\\\\431960\\\\", field=ImageFileName) OR regex("\\\\steamapps\\\\workshop\\\\content\\\\431960\\\\", field=CommandLine)
| NOT ImageFileName=/wallpaper(32|64)\.exe$/i
| NOT ImageFileName=/conhost\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_hash) as hashes values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wallpaper32.exe","wallpaper64.exe") AND (Processes.process_path="*\\steamapps\\workshop\\content\\431960\\*" OR Processes.parent_process="*\\steamapps\\workshop\\content\\431960\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where process_name!="wallpaper32.exe" AND process_name!="wallpaper64.exe"
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_hash) as hashes values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wallpaper32.exe","wallpaper64.exe") AND (Processes.process_path="*\\steamapps\\workshop\\content\\431960\\*" OR Processes.parent_process="*\\steamapps\\workshop\\content\\431960\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where process_name!="wallpaper32.exe" AND process_name!="wallpaper64.exe"
AggregatorHost.dll loaded from non-System32 path (Steam credential stealer sideload) AIInstallation High
Genuine AggregatorHost.dll ships in %WINDIR%\System32\. The article's payload bundles a same-named DLL outside System32 to blend in. Detects any process loading AggregatorHost.dll whose folder path is not the canonical System32 location. Rationale: Article names AggregatorHost.dll specifically as the sideloaded Steam credential stealer. Real AggregatorHost.dll is a tiny Windows .NET host stub in System32 — any other location is high-fidelity. MITRE T1574.002 mapping confirmed against attack.mitre.org. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/002/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developers running locally-built .NET-hosting code that names its host AggregatorHost.dll (very rare)
  • Software-deployment shares (SCCM, Intune Win32 app cache) staging the legitimate DLL under %ProgramData% before copy to System32
  • Restore/repair operations from Windows installation media mounting an offline image
  • Forensic tools or analysts running the DLL from a sandbox path during incident response
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","trustedinstaller.exe","setup.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: hash the loaded DLL, compare SHA256/MD5 to the known-bad list in UC5, and check signature with sigcheck/Get-AuthenticodeSignature — genuine AggregatorHost.dll is Microsoft-signed; the malicious copy will be unsigned or signed by an unfamiliar publisher. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the loading process, quarantine the DLL file and its parent folder (likely a Workshop subfolder under steamapps\workshop\content\431960\). 3) Hunt: enumerate all DeviceFileEvents writes of AggregatorHost.dll in the last 30 days across the fleet, pivot on InitiatingProcessFileName to find every distinct dropper, and check for outbound network connections from the loading process to the article's C2 IPs.
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "AggregatorHost.dll"
| where FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\"
     and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\SysWOW64\"
     and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\WinSxS\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
Event
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Source =~ "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" and EventID == 7
| extend ImageLoaded = tostring(parse_xml(EventData).EventData.Data[5].["#text"])
| extend ProcessImage = tostring(parse_xml(EventData).EventData.Data[4].["#text"])
| extend ImageHashes = tostring(parse_xml(EventData).EventData.Data[11].["#text"])

     and ImageLoaded !startswith @"C:\Windows\SysWOW64\"
     and ImageLoaded !startswith @"C:\Windows\WinSxS\"

| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AggregatorHost.dll Loaded From Non-System32 Path (Wallpaper Engine Sideload)
id: a3f1c4b2-7d8e-4f9a-9b1c-2d4e5f6a7b8c
description: Detects load of AggregatorHost.dll from any folder other than the canonical System32 / SysWOW64 / WinSxS paths, a sideload technique observed in the Steam Workshop Wallpaper Engine credential-theft chain.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/steam-workshop-abused-to-spread-malware-via-wallpaper-engine-app/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.t1574.002
  - attack.t1036.005
logsource:
  category: image_load
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ImageLoaded|endswith: '\AggregatorHost.dll'
  filter_legit:
    ImageLoaded|startswith:
      - 'C:\Windows\System32\'
      - 'C:\Windows\SysWOW64\'
      - 'C:\Windows\WinSxS\'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:7 (@ImageLoaded:*\AggregatorHost.dll OR @ImageLoaded:*\aggregatorhost.dll OR @ImageLoaded:*\AGGREGATORHOST.DLL) -@ImageLoaded:(C\:\\Windows\\System32\\* OR C\:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\* OR C\:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\*)
#event_simpleName=ClassifiedModuleLoad OR #event_simpleName=ImageHash
| TargetFileName=/\\AggregatorHost\.dll$/i
| NOT TargetFileName=/^C:\\Windows\\(System32|SysWOW64|WinSxS)\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
`sysmon` EventCode=7 ImageLoaded="*\\AggregatorHost.dll" NOT (ImageLoaded="*\\Windows\\System32\\AggregatorHost.dll" OR ImageLoaded="*\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\AggregatorHost.dll" OR ImageLoaded="*\\Windows\\WinSxS\\*\\AggregatorHost.dll") | stats min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Image) as loading_process values(Hashes) as dll_hashes count by host ImageLoaded User
Non-Steam process reading Steam sentry / loginusers credential files AIActions on Objectives High
Detects file reads or copies of Steam credential artefacts (ssfn* sentry files, loginusers.vdf, config.vdf) by processes that are not part of the Steam client family. The article calls out Steam account credential theft as the goal of the sideloaded AggregatorHost.dll. Rationale: ssfn* files are Steam's machine-binding sentry tokens — possession means session takeover without the password. loginusers.vdf holds the cached account list. Article explicitly states the goal is to 'search for Steam accounts on the computer and steal account credentials.' Cross-checked Steam credential artefact paths against public Steam Support documentation. Cross-checked against: • https://help.steampowered.com/en/faqs/view/65A9-CFE7-2369-A0A8 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/
ATT&CKT1555 T1539 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Backup utilities (Acronis, Veeam Agent, Macrium) capturing user profile data including the Steam config folder
  • AV/EDR products scanning the Steam config folder during a full filesystem sweep
  • Steam beta launcher variants or third-party Steam family-sharing tools that legitimately read ssfn files
  • Forensic acquisition tools (FTK Imager, KAPE) being run by IR or sysadmins
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("backup.exe","veeamagent.exe","acronis_loader.exe","mscsweep.exe","MsMpEng.exe","kape.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify InitiatingProcessFileName and its SHA256; if it's an unsigned binary under steamapps\workshop\content\431960\ this is almost certainly the article's stealer. Grab a copy of the file for malware analysis. 2) Contain: isolate the host, force-log out the affected Steam account via Steam Account Security (deauthorize all devices), invalidate the user's Steam password and Steam Guard recovery codes, and remove the malicious wallpaper Workshop subscription. 3) Hunt: pivot on the dropper SHA256 across the fleet, query UC2 (AggregatorHost.dll sideload) and UC4 (C2 connections) for the same host, and check Steam community trade/market activity for the user's account in the last 7 days for asset theft.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
     or FolderPath has @"\Steam\config\"
| where FileName matches regex @"(?i)^(loginusers\.vdf|config\.vdf|ssfn[0-9]+)$"
     or FolderPath has @"\Steam\config\"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("steam.exe","steamservice.exe","steamwebhelper.exe","gameoverlayui.exe","streaming_client.exe","steamerrorreporter.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\Steam\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^(loginusers\.vdf|config\.vdf|ssfn[0-9]+)$"
   or TargetFilePath has @"\Steam\config\"
| where not (ActingProcessName has_any ("steam.exe","steamservice.exe","steamwebhelper.exe","gameoverlayui.exe","streaming_client.exe","steamerrorreporter.exe"))
| where not (ActingProcessCommandLine has @"\Steam\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Non-Steam Process Accessing Steam Credential Artefacts
id: 7b9c1d2e-3f4a-5b6c-7d8e-9f0a1b2c3d4e
description: Detects file access to Steam sentry (ssfn*), loginusers.vdf, or config.vdf by processes outside the Steam client family — the credential-theft step of the Steam Workshop Wallpaper Engine campaign.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/steam-workshop-abused-to-spread-malware-via-wallpaper-engine-app/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16

  - attack.t1539

  product: windows

  filter_steam:

      - '\steam.exe'
      - '\steamservice.exe'
      - '\steamwebhelper.exe'
      - '\gameoverlayui.exe'
      - '\streaming_client.exe'

  condition: selection_files and not filter_steam
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:*\loginusers.vdf OR @TargetFilename:*\LoginUsers.vdf OR @TargetFilename:*\config.vdf OR @TargetFilename:*\Config.vdf OR @TargetFilename:*\ssfn* OR @TargetFilename:*\Steam\config\*) -@Image:(*\steam.exe OR *\Steam.exe OR *\steamservice.exe OR *\steamwebhelper.exe OR *\gameoverlayui.exe OR *\GameOverlayUI.exe OR *\streaming_client.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/(\\loginusers\.vdf|\\config\.vdf|\\ssfn[0-9]+|\\Steam\\config\\)/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(steam|steamservice|steamwebhelper|gameoverlayui|streaming_client|steamerrorreporter)\.exe$/i
| NOT regex("\\\\Steam\\\\", field=ContextImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())

Outbound connection to Steam Workshop wallpaper campaign C2 (202.144.192.29 / 120.48.156.17 / brightly.to) AICommand & Control High
Network beacon to the three article-named C2 endpoints used by the DarkKomet backdoor / AggregatorHost stealer / Lumma / Vidar / RanEngine payloads delivered through malicious Wallpaper Engine wallpapers. Any internal host contacting these is high-confidence compromise. Rationale: All three indicators are named directly in the kill-chain reconstruction for the same campaign and tied to multiple distinct payload families (DarkKomet, AggregatorHost, Lumma, Vidar, RanEngine). No second-source corroboration yet (campaign just published), so confidence relies on the Kaspersky attribution; treat any internal hit as a confirmed-compromise pivot.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel feed validation traffic from a security tool (e.g. analyst sandbox detonation hitting the C2)
  • Researcher VM intentionally browsing brightly.to for analysis
  • Shared-hosting provider parking the IP on an unrelated benign domain (verify reverse DNS)
  • Outbound proxy / SASE service health-checking a blocklisted URL
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","falcon-sensor.exe","sentinelagent.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify which internal hosts connected and which user/process initiated; pull InitiatingProcessFileName & InitiatingProcessFolderPath — if process lives under steamapps\workshop\content\431960\ this is the article's chain. 2) Contain: block 202.144.192.29, 120.48.156.17, and *.brightly.to at egress firewall + DNS sinkhole; isolate the originating hosts via EDR network containment; force-revoke Steam Guard tokens and reset Steam passwords for affected users. 3) Hunt: run UC1/UC2/UC3 across the same DeviceId for the previous 30 days, search DeviceFileEvents for the hashes in UC5, and pivot from the originating process SHA256 across the fleet to find any other host with the same dropper.
let C2_IPs = dynamic(["202.144.192.29","120.48.156.17"]);
let C2_Domains = dynamic(["brightly.to"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (C2_IPs)
   or RemoteUrl has_any (C2_Domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let C2_IPs = dynamic(["202.144.192.29","120.48.156.17"]);
let C2_Domains = dynamic(["brightly.to"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (ImNetworkSession
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DstIpAddr in (C2_IPs) or DstHostname in~ (C2_Domains) or Url has_any (C2_Domains)
        | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, User=SrcUsername, Process=tostring(parse_json("")), RemoteIP=DstIpAddr, RemoteUrl=coalesce(DstHostname, Url)),
    (ImDnsActivity
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DnsQuery in~ (C2_Domains)
        | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, User=SrcUsername, Process="", RemoteIP="", RemoteUrl=DnsQuery),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DestinationIP in (C2_IPs) or RequestURL has_any (C2_Domains) or DestinationDnsDomain has_any (C2_Domains)
        | project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, User=SourceUserName, Process=DestinationProcessName, RemoteIP=DestinationIP, RemoteUrl=coalesce(RequestURL, DestinationDnsDomain))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Known DarkKomet / Wallpaper-Engine campaign payload hash execution or write AIInstallation Medium
Detects execution or file-write of any of the 13 article-named MD5s tied to the malicious wallpaper bundles (DarkKomet droppers, AggregatorHost.dll variants, Lumma/Vidar/RanEngine stages). Pure IOC hunt; will catch any host that downloaded a known-bad Workshop package even if behaviour-based UCs missed it. Rationale: All 13 MD5s are taken verbatim from the article's pre-extracted IOC bundle covering the DarkKomet droppers and AggregatorHost.dll sideload payloads. 90-day lookback because some Workshop subscriptions sit on disk for weeks before installation/launch.
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1027.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware-analysis sandbox or research VM in the fleet legitimately running known-bad samples
  • EDR / SOAR auto-detonation pipeline (e.g. ANY.RUN connector) leaving sample artefacts on a SOC host
  • Threat-intel vendor agent caching a sample for offline scanning
  • Old quarantine restore on an analyst workstation pulling a sample for reverse engineering
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm hit isn't an analyst sandbox; pull DeviceName, FolderPath, parent process and timeline of the file write — chase upstream to find the wallpaper Workshop item id (the path under steamapps\workshop\content\431960\<id>\). 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill any running process matching the hash, quarantine the file system-wide via Defender Indicator (FileHash → BlockAndRemediate), push the 13 hashes to corporate AV/EDR blocklists. 3) Hunt: run UC4 (C2 IPs) and UC3 (Steam credential file access) against the affected host for the last 90 days; submit the Workshop item id (and author Steam ID) to Valve security via steamcommunity.com/dev for takedown; query CrowdStrike / Defender across the fleet for any other host with these MD5s on disk even without execution.
let BadMD5 = dynamic(["95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068","af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a","c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf","d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da","8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854","b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09","ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1","20965254e29104986e11939decd39549","18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883","0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d","5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355","fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6","74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
        | where MD5 in (BadMD5) or InitiatingProcessMD5 in (BadMD5)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source="Process", FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, MD5, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath),
    (DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
        | where MD5 in (BadMD5)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="FileWrite", FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, MD5, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath),
    (DeviceImageLoadEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
        | where MD5 in (BadMD5)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="DllLoad", FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, MD5, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath=InitiatingProcessFolderPath)
| order by Timestamp desc
let BadMD5 = dynamic(["95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068","af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a","c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf","d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da","8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854","b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09","ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1","20965254e29104986e11939decd39549","18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883","0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d","5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355","fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6","74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
        | where MD5 in (BadMD5)
        | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, User=ActorUsername, Source="Process", FileName=TargetProcessName, CommandLine=TargetProcessCommandLine, MD5, SHA256),
    (ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
        | where TargetFileMD5 in (BadMD5) or Hash in (BadMD5)
        | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, User=ActorUsername, Source="FileEvent", FileName=TargetFileName, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, MD5=TargetFileMD5, SHA256=TargetFileSHA256),
    (SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
        | where EventID == 4688
        | where FileHash has_any (BadMD5)
        | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, User=SubjectUserName, Source="4688", FileName=NewProcessName, CommandLine=CommandLine, MD5=FileHash, SHA256="")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

(| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_name) as process from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_hash IN ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068","af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a","c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf","d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da","8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854","b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09","ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1","20965254e29104986e11939decd39549","18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883","0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d","5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355","fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6","74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`)
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or SHA1 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or MD5 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or SHA1 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or MD5 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

The Hacker News
2026-06-16 18 use cases 9 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected
